No in-app chat exists [F3]; the driver denies impropriety and admits only small talk [F4]; no system record corroborates or rebuts either account. SAFE-1 mandates human handling and no automated verdict or amount. Reviewer to note: allegation is verbal and uncorroborated [F3][F4]; both profiles clean (rider F5; driver F6); GPS shows no deviation (−0.1 km, F1) and a fixed $35.84 fare (F2), so no monetary remedy is in issue. Advise rider of 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your report has been sent to a RydeHELP human safety reviewer. Because it describes comments of a personal and sexual nature and a request for your number, it must be handled by a person, not decided automatically. The reviewer will look at your statement and the driver's response, along with the trip details. Nothing in the trip record independently confirms or disproves either account, so the reviewer will weigh both. No fare change is being made. You can also reach out anytime: call 995 for urgent medical help, and RydeHELP to report this or get support.

DRIVER: The rider's report from your late-night trip has been sent to a RydeHELP human safety reviewer; you do not need to respond again now. Because the account describes a verbal exchange, this cannot be decided automatically. The reviewer will look at the rider's statement and your response, plus the trip details. Nothing in the trip record independently confirms or disproves either account. No fare change is being made, and no action is being taken on your account at this stage. If you have anything further to add, contact RydeHELP.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer case B-0047 to RydeHELP human safety review: rider alleges verbal body comments and an unsolicited request for her number during a late-night RydeX trip (22:29–22:54); no in-app chat exists so no system record corroborates or rebuts either account. Human reviewer to take the rider's statement (F5 context) and driver's denial (F4) as an unresolved factual conflict, and to advise the rider of the 995 / driver commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths. Do not issue any fare adjustment.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute type is safety and the rider alleges the driver commented on her body and asked for her number, which she experienced as harassment. That allegation is content in the complaint record, and a threat/intimidation/harassment allegation in the complaint triggers the no-automated-verdict rule [F4][SAFE-1]. The policy's safety rule turns on such content appearing in the chat, the complaint or the driver statement, and it does not require a keyword-flagged in-app message; the complaint in this file is itself the triggering content [F4][SAFE-1]. Whether or not any keyword table flags it must go to human handling [SAFE-1].

The record cannot resolve the one-to-one conflict: there are no in-app messages at all in this case [F3], so whatever was said was verbal and there is no contemporaneous system record. The driver's statement denies anything inappropriate and describes only small talk [F4]; a user statement of this kind neither proves nor disproves the allegation. Under the safety rule this unresolved verbal-conduct conflict is exactly what is reserved for human review, not an automated finding [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The trip data show no irregularity that could ground any monetary remedy. Actual distance was 17.2 km against an optimal route of 17.3 km, i.e. −0.1 km (−0%), which yields no off-route segment at all, so no deviation liability and no detour refund arise for this RydeX fixed fare [F1][RD-1][RD-2]. Duration was 25.9 min against a 24-min estimate (+2.3 min) [F2], and the fare was a fixed quoted $35.84 with no fare fact showing any unpublished add-on, so there is nothing to refund under the fare rules either [F2][FARE-1].

Both profiles are clean in the relevant window: the rider has 1656 days of account history with 0 disputes and 0 upheld in the last 90 days [F5], and the driver has 1392 days, 4.8 rating, 659 trips with 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F6]. Profile facts cannot decide a case on their own; here they neither corroborate the allegation nor establish a pattern of misconduct, so no account-review action is supported [F5][F6][RD-6].

For a safety matter no automated ruling or amount is issued. No monetary remedy is computable in any event given the GPS shows no deviation (−0.1 km) and the fare was fixed [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2][FARE-1]. The matter is referred to a human reviewer, who should note: the dispute occurred on a late-night trip picked up 22:29 and dropped off 22:54 [F2]; the allegation is verbal, with no in-app thread [F3]; the driver admits only small talk and denies impropriety [F4]; the rider's clean record [F5] bears on context but no system record independently supports either account [F3][F4]. Reviewer to follow SAFE-related reporting paths (995 for medical assistance, driver commercial insurance for claims, RydeHELP for reporting).

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that SAFE-1 is not engaged because the chat record carries no keyword-flagged content is rejected: SAFE-1's trigger is harassing content appearing in the chat, the complaint or the driver statement, and the rider's complaint of body comments and a request for her number is such content [F4]; the absence of an in-app thread [F3] removes the evidence, not the trigger [SAFE-1].

The claim that the driver's clean profile forecloses any further action goes beyond what the profile can do: the driver's 1392-day, 659-trip, zero-dispute record cannot decide a verbal-conduct allegation and, since no route or fare violation is established on this trip [F1][F2], no RD-6 account-review condition is met [F6][RD-6].

The claim that there is no fare or deviation component is accepted on the numbers, but it does not dispose of the case: the GPS shows no off-route segment [F1][RD-1] and the fare was a fixed $35.84 with no unpublished add-on shown [F2][FARE-1], yet the safety allegation in F4 still requires human review and is not answered by the absence of a refund [SAFE-1].

The rider's clean 90-day history [F5] cannot be used as corroboration of the alleged conduct; profile facts do not decide a case and the complaint content in F4 is the operative trigger for human review, not the rider's record [F5][SAFE-1].

The driver's 659-trip, zero-dispute profile [F6] cannot be used either way to decide the credibility contest or to support an account flag; no RD-6 condition (no upheld violation in this case) is met, so profile facts remain context only [F6][RD-6].

claims.assertion: This is a safety/harassment dispute: the rider reports the driver made comments about her body and asked for her number, which she experienced as harassment and felt unsafe — conduct that Ryde's Code of Conduct treats as a zero-tolerance violation requiring human handling rather than an automated fare ruling.

The driver's written statement admits only that he 'made small talk' and denies anything inappropriate; the case therefore turns on an unresolved factual conflict about in-trip conduct, which is exactly the situation SAFE-1 reserves for human review rather than automated decision.

There is no in-app chat history between rider and driver, so the reported comments were verbal and cannot be corroborated or rebutted by any system record; no clause in the policy allows a verbal statement to be resolved by GPS, timeline or fare data.

The trip itself shows no irregularity that would distract from the safety issue: actual distance 17.2 km against an optimal 17.3 km (-0.1 km, -0%) and duration 25.9 min against 24 min estimated (+2.3 min), i.e. no route deviation and hence no fare or routing claim is available to the rider.

The rider has a 4.5-year account with a 4.86 rating and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in the last 90 days, which bears on her credibility as the complainant in a verbal-conduct case where no other record exists.

The driver has 659 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes or upheld disputes in the same window; this cuts both ways, so it cannot be used to decide the credibility contest and further supports routing the matter to human review instead of an automated finding.

weaknesses: There is no in-app chat evidence at all (F3): if the comments were verbal, the rider's account rests on her complaint alone, with no message, threat keyword or other system record behind it.

The driver's statement (F4) denies any inappropriate conduct, and the policy gives no evidentiary rule for resolving a one-to-one verbal conflict; a human reviewer may find the rider's recollection uncorroborated.

No supporting system data exists — no fare facts and no traffic facts were returned, and the GPS facts (F1, F2) show a normal trip, so nothing in the record independently corroborates the alleged conduct.
Both parties' 90-day histories are clean (F5, F6: 0 disputes, 0 upheld each) and profile facts may not be used to decide the case, so no prior-incident pattern can bolster the rider's account.

claims.assertion: This is a safety-type dispute; the only chat-fact record is the driver's statement that he made small talk and that nothing inappropriate happened, and no in-app message (no threat, request or agreement tag) exists on the record.

SAFE-1 is triggered only by threatening, intimidating, harassing or sexually harassing content appearing in chat records, complaints or driver statements; the chat record here contains no such keyword-flagged content, so the mandatory escalate rule is not engaged by the chat facts.

No traffic/weather facts exist for this trip, and the route taken was actually 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route (17.2 km vs 17.3 km, -0%), so no off-route segment and no route-based liability can be established against the driver.

The driver has 1392 days of account history, a 4.8 rating over 659 trips in the last 90 days, and zero disputes filed or upheld (route 0, no-show 0), so there is no profile record of misconduct, recurring harassment or abuse warranting a flag_account action.

The rider's profile shows 1656 days of account history, a 4.86 rating and 0 disputes in 90 days, so the rider's history gives no corroboration beyond the complaint itself; the complaint statement is the sole source of the harassment allegation.

The trip was completed as booked: 17.2 km in 25.9 min against a 24-min estimate (+2.3 min) on a fixed $35.84 RydeX fare, so there is no fare or deviation component to refund and the complaint cannot produce a monetary remedy.

weaknesses: The complainant's account of the comments and the request for her number is a first-person harassment allegation and is exactly the kind of content SAFE-1 is designed to capture; it is not rebutted by any system record, because thread B-0047 has no in-app chat (F3) and the driver's denial (F4) is a user-submitted statement that loses to nothing but also proves nothing.

The absence of in-app chat (F3) cuts both ways: it explains why no threat keyword was flagged, but it also means the driver has no contemporaneous evidence supporting his version — the conversation, if it happened, occurred verbally in the cabin where no system record exists.

The ride was the late-night trip at 22:29 and lasted 25.9 min (F2), and there is no rider-side history of unfounded complaints (F5) that could be used to suggest the allegation is fabricated, so the driver cannot point to any fact undermining the rider's credibility.

Safety allegations fall outside the automated-verdict scheme and are referred to human review by design; the driver should expect escalation and an evidence-based human assessment rather than a dismissal, since a mismatch between a complaint and the chat record is not proof of innocence.

points.response: Conceded in the narrow sense that the only chat-file entry is the driver's denial (F4) with no in-app thread (F3) — but that is precisely why the file cannot resolve the conflict, and SAFE-1 takes the content of the complaint, not the tag on a message, as its trigger.

SAFE-1 is not keyword-gated: it is engaged where threatening, intimidating, harassing or sexually harassing content appears in chat, the complaint or the driver's statement, and the complaint here alleges body comments and a request for the rider's number (F4), so the escalate rule is triggered.
Accepted and not contested by the rider: the GPS record shows 17.2 km versus an optimal 17.3 km (-0.1 km, -0%) with no off-route segment (F1), so the rider makes no route-deviation claim.

The rider does not ask for flag_account on the driver's account; a clean 90-day profile (F6) simply means profile facts decide nothing here, and SAFE-1 still requires the conduct allegation itself to go to human review.

The rider's clean record (F5) is not offered as corroboration of the event — it is offered against the suggestion of a fabricated complaint, and no policy clause permits an uncorroborated verbal conflict to be dismissed for want of a system record.

The rider claims no monetary remedy: the ride ran 17.2 km in 25.9 min against a 24-min estimate on a fixed fare (F1, F2), so the only relief sought is the human safety review that SAFE-1 mandates for the allegations in F4.

Not contested as to the outcome: SAFE-1 forbids an automated verdict on a harassment allegation and the only in-app chat record here, F3, contains no threat-flagged content, so the case must go to human review — which is also what my client asks for (escalate, no monetary finding against either party). F4 is a user-submitted statement and cannot itself establish that the Code of Conduct was breached.

Accepted as far as it goes: the driver's statement is exactly what F4 records — 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened' — and SAFE-1 sends the resulting one-to-one factual conflict to human handling rather than to an automated finding, so I do not ask the judge to resolve it in the driver's favour.

Agreed, and this is the core of my client's position: F3 shows no in-app messages at all, so any exchange was verbal and no chat-threat record exists; SAFE-1's trigger is content in the chat/complaint/statement record, and the chat record here carries none, so the mandatory escalate is precautionary rather than a finding.

Accepted, and it confirms there is nothing in the trip data to refund or to attribute to the driver: F1 shows 17.2 km against a 17.3 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -%) and F2 shows 25.9 min against a 24-min estimate, so no RD-1 deviation and no RD-2/FARE-1 amount is computable.

Profile facts cannot decide the case: F5 (rider, 1656 days, 4.86, 0 disputes) may bear on context, but under the policy a clean profile neither proves nor rebuts a verbal-conduct allegation, so it cannot convert F4 into a finding against my client.

Agreed that F6 cuts both ways and cannot decide credibility; it is precisely why I ask for escalate and expressly do not request a flag_account against the rider, my client's 1392-day, 659-trip, zero-dispute record (F6) being offered only as rebuttal to any abuse-of-account suggestion.
